item.description:
## 一个反直觉的观察：Ming-Yu Liu 的"低 ego"，其实是 NVIDIA 商业模式的产物，而不是修行的结果
多数人会把他反复强调的"不竞争、不追第一、帮所有人成功"解读为一种个人修养的成熟。但如果你把 NVIDIA 的商业结构叠加上去，会发现一个几乎冷酷的事实：**NVIDIA 是全球唯一一家"下游对手越多、自己赚得越多"的 AI 公司。** 他所有的世界观——Cosmos 开源、把机器人公司当客户不当对手、不做端到端产品、认为模型能力必然收敛——本质上都不是哲学，而是**卖铲人视角下最优的经营策略**。所以他能说出"我没有对手"，是因为他站在整个生态最上游的地基上；而一个 Frontier Lab 的研究者，就算再想低 ego，也做不到——他的每一次 benchmark 落后，都是股价、融资和团队士气的直接扣分。
**换句话说：低 ego 不是一种性格，而是一种奢侈。它需要你所在位置的博弈结构支持它。**
## 跨领域连接：这场访谈里出现了三个"信息瓶颈"——它们其实是同一件事
一个很少有人指出的模式：Ming-Yu 讲的三件看似无关的事，底层是同一个结构。

item.title: [Zhang Xiaojun Podcast] 150. 对英伟达研究副总裁刘洺堉的4小时访谈：功夫、Cosmos 3、开源世界模型、黄仁勋、你不需要击败所有对手
item.dc:creator: Zhang Xiaojun Podcast
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、最出人意料的观察：功夫拳理竟是他管理300人团队的底层操作系统

刘洺堉在访谈里轻描淡写地提到自己练八极拳几十年——师承徐纪，祖师是"神枪李书文"。这看起来是纯粹的个人爱好，但如果你把八极拳的核心心法和他管理 Cosmos 团队的方式并置来看，会发现一件惊人的事：他管理团队的哲学，就是把武术的"整劲"外化成了组织形态。

八极拳的核心秘密是：一拳的力量必须从脚起、由腰传、贯于指尖，"发生在一瞬间"却要求全身长路径的高度协调。而他反复强调 Cosmos 团队的两难："每个人的目标要一致，但每个人都要能独立决策"——这正是"整劲"在组织学上的完美对偶。传统管理要么强调 top-down（有整体但每一节僵硬），要么强调 bottom-up（每一节灵活但无整劲）。他找到的解，其实就是拳理里那句"节节贯穿、周身一家"。

更妙的是——他自己说练武是为了"控制自己"，而不是击败别人。这直接对应了他后来对 NVIDIA 竞争哲学的表述："我们不做鱿鱼游戏"。功夫是内向的、非对抗的自我修炼，而他把这种"高手不比武、只求内在完备"的姿态原封不动搬进了顶级 AI 竞赛。

二、被忽略的隐藏创伤：贝尔实验室式衰败是他所有研究策略的暗层代码

访谈中他讲了一个几乎被听众划过的故事：他 2012 年加入的 MERL（三菱电机研究所）里的老前辈，很多来自 Bell Labs / 30 Electronics 那一批被解散的传奇研究员——Bill Freeman、Alyosha Efros 等人。他亲眼看到 Blue Sky Research 曾经的圣殿如何轰然坍塌。

这个创伤性认知塑造了他此后每一个重大决策的底色：他向 Jensen 要 1000 张 A100 时要写"letter"论证商业价值；他把 Picasso 关停转投 Cosmos；他每次强调"研究要 align 公司"。表面上是理性的战略，但底下是一个亲历过学术乌托邦崩溃的人的自保本能。

跨领域连接：这与经济学里的"大萧条一代"（Depression-era generation）行为模式高度同构——经历过系统崩溃的人，一辈子都在做反脆弱的投资决策，即使处在丰饶时代。他之所以能在 NVIDIA 从研究员爬到 VP，恰恰是因为他从来不是"纯研究员"——Bell Labs 的骨灰给了他一种其他 AI 研究员没有的组织免疫力。

三、"22 变 1"是他整个职业生涯的分形

最有趣的是他讲 Jensen 用 LV 门店举例劝他把 22 个模型合并的那段：奢侈品店越简化陈列，消费者越容易决策。但如果你倒回来看他所有的技术选择——这不是一次孤立事件，而是他大脑里跑了 20 年的同一个压缩算法：

  • 早期 CV 各种手工特征 → GAN 一统
  • GAN 各种 loss trick → Diffusion
  • Cosmos 1 有 22 个模型 → Cosmos 3 一个 omni-model
  • 甚至他自己反复说的话："事情越变越简单，找到本质"

而这与他反复引用费曼那句 "If I cannot create, I cannot understand" 形成一个绝妙的闭环：创造是理解的证明，而理解的极致就是能用最少的模型描述最多的世界。所以 Cosmos 3 不只是一个技术选择，它是他 20 年"寻找本质"这条个人叙事线的收束时刻。

跨领域连接：这几乎就是物理学史的微缩版本——从托勒密的 80 个本轮 → 开普勒的三定律 → 牛顿的一个 F=ma。每一次 AI 范式转移，本质上都是在重演一次科学史的"奥卡姆剃刀"事件。 他自觉不自觉地把自己放进了这条谱系里。

四、隐藏在"低 ego"话术下的反身性优势

他反复说自己"low ego"、"不追求击败别人"、"帮生态成功"。听起来像是政治正确的公关辞令。但仔细拆解，你会发现这是一个精算过的博弈策略：

当你是基础设施提供者，把自己定义为"竞争者"是自杀。 因为你只要跟客户竞争一次，所有客户都会开始怀疑你。所以"low ego"不是道德姿态，而是 NVIDIA 商业模式的必然产物——你必须真诚地帮所有人赢，才能让他们放心把命脉交给你的 GPU 和 CUDA。

而这个逻辑投射到 Cosmos 上就变成了一个非常锋利的产品哲学："我做的模型不是产品，是让别人做产品的底座"。你注意到没有——他从头到尾没有说过任何一个"打败 Sora"、"超过 Veo"之类的话。他甚至真诚地为 Tim Brooks 高兴。这种姿态在这个时代的 AI 圈稀有到几乎反常。

而最终极的启示是："零亿美元生意"这个 Jensen 反复挂在嘴边的概念，本质上是把"避开竞争"变成了公司战略的第一性原理。 存量市场必然内卷，但如果你专门做"现在没有、未来会巨大"的市场，你就永远不需要打赢别人。这是《创新者的窘境》的镜像操作——不是被颠覆者的悲剧，而是主动跳到下一片蓝海的选择。

📝 转录文本

对英伟达研究副总裁刘洺堉的4小时访谈

开场介绍

Hello everyone, I'm Xiaojun. Today I'm in Shanghai, and the person I'm talking to is the Vice President of NVIDIA Research, Liu Mingyu. Our conversation time is one month after Huang Renxun just visited China.

Mingyu has always given me a very simple outfit, carrying an old shoe bag, and a very friendly attitude. But the people in NVIDIA told me that he is not a typical researcher, but more like a leader in engineering. Huang Renxun gave him an evaluation: GSD, Getting Shit Done.

Not long ago, Liu Mingyu's team just released the world model of NVIDIA, Cosmos 3. So in this interview, we will talk about Cosmos 3, the world model, and also talk about a researcher who has been in the club for 20 years. And this researcher's identity is very special. He is in a huge system of basic facilities like NVIDIA. This changed his many research ideas. Of course, we also talked about some of the stories about NVIDIA and Huang Renxun.

Mingyu said that making a model should be low ego. Model competition shouldn't be a game.

几个关键的观点先行

"Jensen often talks about how he likes this kind of zero billion dollar business. You cannot make money, but when the business is successful, influential."

"The degree of economic growth is based on how much money is left in one person's pocket. The degree of research should be based on how much ideas are left in another person's head."

"When we finished Cosmos 1, we asked Jensen if he wanted to continue doing it. Jensen told me that I should continue doing Cosmos 1到97."

"He is a very disciplined person. Some things are very important. He will teach you to pace your steps. He is good at doing marathon. He thinks the company will be bankrupt in 30 days."

问：You have joined NVIDIA for 10 years. 答：Yes. 问：How many times have you changed in NVIDIA in the past 10 years?

打招呼与来华行程

问： Hello Mingyu, how about you say hi to the audience first?

答： Hello everyone, I'm Liu Mingyu.

问： 我们刚聊到你在美国 20 年、在英伟达 10 年，你现在在公司说很多中文吗？

答： Sometimes I speak Chinese, but most of the time I still speak English. Because most of the time, many people in the team don't speak Chinese. So communication is mainly in English. But if you participate in a small group meeting, you speak Chinese. Then naturally, you will switch to the Chinese mode.

问： What is your trip to China like this time? How long will you come to China?

答： I come to China about 2-3 times a year. Because the main task given by my company and my personal interest is Physical AI. In China, the development of Physical AI is very rapid. Many companies and researchers are making major breakthroughs. We are here to communicate with everyone and understand how we can help them.

问： 这次来感觉到有什么不一样吗，跟之前？

答： 这次来我看到的是越来越多的关于手、灵巧手，在这个关键的科技上面做出突破，然后去追求下一个 Physical AI 可以达到的一些重点能力。

Cosmos Lab 与团队规模

I'm a co-founder of Cosmos Labs. The team consists of researchers and engineers, about 80-90 people. The other team is also working on Cosmos. It's called Dotted Line. Although they didn't report to me directly, I'm the overall pick of the mission. I'm the one who sends the orders and decides the direction. So these people follow my instructions, cooperate with the entire team, and push the target out. There should be between 200 and 300 people working on Cosmos.

问： I saw you manage a team called Deep Imagination Research Group before. Is Cosmos a part of it? What is their relationship?

答： Yes, I joined NVIDIA about 10 years ago. When I joined NVIDIA, my goal was to give job talk to NVIDIA. When I was selling myself to NVIDIA, my job talk was about 4 years ago. I was talking about one day, the most important thing to generate video computing will be deep learning, not traditional computer graphics.

In those days, computer special effects, movie special effects, using this traditional graphics pipeline to generate beautiful graphics was mainstream. I thought deep learning was the trend of the future in the early days of this field.

I remember at that time, I talked to our chief scientist, Bill Dally, during the presentation. My presentation was about deep learning, because it's data-driven. It can do a lot of things that traditional graphers can't do. For example, one day I can use a novel as an input and put it into deep learning to produce a movie.

At that time, I was very interested in this thing. I was honored to join NVIDIA. After entering, I continued to work in this direction.

GAN 时代：从对抗生成网络到 GauGAN

In that period, the most important model was Generative Adversarial Network. I was the one who was in the field of anti-rebellion network research in the early days. I did a few jobs that I felt proud of.

One of them is called unsupervised or unpaired image translation. In AI, a lot of times you learn by supervision. You need the corresponding input and output to learn the input-output relationship. Unsupervised means you don't have the corresponding input-output. You don't know what happens when this person laughs. You don't know what happens when this code becomes a password. We used some information bottlenecks to create this on-site image-to-image translation.

When I joined NVIDIA, NVIDIA was not an AI company that everyone recognized. Deep learning was not as popular as it is now. NVIDIA traditionally did computer architecture to design GPU. No one is doing this kind of application-oriented research. I was doing this direction early on.

Then one of the works is called GauGAN. It's like a small painter painting a few colors. Each color represents a different language. After you paint it, it can become a beautiful mountain painting. That work allows me to help NVIDIA establish an image that can not only produce good GPUs, but also produce good AI models.

At that time, I had some colleagues doing research in the direction of StyleGAN. We are the group of people who put NVIDIA from DEP as the first one to do this kind of media generation on the deep-level network.

After a while, 那时候公司就觉得我可以了，然后就可以开始成立自己的团队。那我那时候成立的团队就叫 the Imagination Research，就是跟我当初给 job talk 的目标是一致。

问： 这是哪一年？

答： 19 到 20 年之间，那时候我变成一个 Research Director。就是那时候知道自己要成立团队，就跟着几个一起工作的伙伴，开始建立这个 Deep Imagination Research。

从数字人到 DALL·E 的觉醒

After Deep Imagination Research, I have been solving related problems step by step. I want to put novels into the film and create a film goal. We did a few interesting demos.

One year, our CEO Jensen wanted to use a digital person to replace him for the keynote. So we did a fake Jensen keynote demo for him. And then it continued. During the pandemic, digital people have been developing very well, and we also contributed some of the technologies that we are proud of.

When I was giving Job Talk ten years ago, I wanted to solve the topic of novels turning into movies. But at that time, I felt that this topic might take a long time to solve. I should say that I didn't realize at that time that we actually have this condition. When my computing and data were sufficient, I could make such a big breakthrough. But at that time, I was busy doing digital people and doing various interesting applications.

One day, OpenAI released this DALL·E, the earliest text-to-image model. I realized that my ambition was not big enough. I was not brave enough. I was not determined to do this. In the most calculated place.

At that time, NVIDIA was operating like this. You want Jensen to invest in your calculation. You want to say why this is important to the company.

I remember when DALL·E came out at that time, I wrote a letter to Jensen. Tell him that in the future, it's very clear that we're going to do this image production with Deep Learning. Many clients use NVIDIA GPUs and traditional graphics to do this image production. We can't go backward with Deep Learning to do image production. We must invest in GPUs to help this field grow.

Picasso 项目与 AI Foundry

During that time, I also had a lot of collaborations with Getty Images because I've always been doing this direction. These traditional content companies are also very interested in AI. But they just try it out, but they don't have enough determination.

After seeing the example, I wrote a letter to Jensen asking for GPU. I wrote a letter to Getty Images saying we should cooperate, so that you can have more security in the future.

Then we talked about this cooperation plan: they provide data, then we have the computing power, then we build this big model to do this text-to-image. This is the time point for me to step into the big model.

At that time, we established a project called Picasso. Our goal is to do AI Foundry. Some companies have data, but they don't have AI talent, and they don't have AI infrastructure. But they have data and they have customers. We will make a Gen AI model for them, and then give them the model to build their customers, and then we will make a profit together.

At that time, we did this with Getty Image and Shutterstock. From here, my research not only produced a model, not only produced a paper, but also produced a product that can help the customer succeed. That's how the development of the team was gradually developed. I thought I was determined to start a business.

问： 就是因为挑战最困难的问题？

答： 嗯。因为已经跟 Jensen 要了 GPU。

问： 当时要了多少 GPU 啊？

答： 那时候我是要了 1000 个 A100 GPU。

问： 当时 1000 张很多吗？

答： 是非常的多，那时候还在 NPS 的时代，1000 张已经很多。要把 1000 张的 GPU 串在一起做一个高效的训练也不容易。我们那时候尝试就是遇到很多瓶颈，主力克服。因为我是最早一批去做 GenAI 的，在 Computer Vision 里面做 GenAI 的人。

与 Tim Brooks（Sora 团队）的合作

I am very honored to work with many excellent partners. Many young people who were still in their early years would come to my office to do internships, including Yu Jiahui from Meta, who is now working on Sora's team books. They are all written here.

I remember when Tim Brooks joined my team, he always wanted to make videos and make things that he wanted to make. But at that time, we didn't have technology. We used GAN to work together. At that time, I saw his determination and enthusiasm. Of course, he is very smart and quick. I learned a lot from working with him. We wrote a pretty good paper. After graduating, I wanted to keep him. But he went to OpenAI. I was also very happy that he got a good development in OpenAI.

Then I did this work with Sora. After the work with Sora came out, I was very happy. But I think I still don't have enough determination. Still not enough.

Cosmos 项目的诞生

At that time, we were all doing this field, and we wrote a letter to the whole city saying that we need more funding. This is the origin of the Cosmos project.

Our group of scholars, I and the three FIDs, and our company's Nemo team, Brian Cannarato. Jun Fan was also in the meeting. We discussed and decided to do this world model. We think this is an important technology for the company and for humans.

And then, Jensen asked me and Syafi to do the Cosmo effort. At that time, it wasn't called Cosmos. We knew we were doing the World Simulator. And then, Jensen asked us to think about it: What should we call this project?

We all went back and thought about it. I forgot that there were a few names to choose from. But at the end, Justin said, "Call it Cosmos." We thought the name Cosmos was very good. So the Cosmos project was born.

I was still in the Deep Imagination Lab. At that time, I was originally working on Picasso and AI Foundry for Media Generation. But at the same time, I'm also responsible for Cosmos. I thought that Cosmos project is more important to the company and the whole industry.

分身乏力，没办法同时跑两个重大的 project，然后慢慢就把这个 Picasso 这个 project 给收起来，那帮这些客户找到的其他可以继续支援他们的科技公司。那我就前进开始做 Cosmos。

那 Cosmos 做一段时间，从一做到二做到三，使用它的客户越来越多，需要一定的规模才能去把 Cosmo 这个 project 做好。

你可以想我在 research 时期可能就是像一个萌芽阶段，当然现在这个 Cosmo 已经被这么多人给依赖，不管是外面的客户或者是公司内部的团队，到一个不能死，就是一定要成功的一个阶段，那所需要的资源更加的庞大。

就是在今年年初的时候，我就从 Media Research 离开了。我现在是 report 给我们的 Senior VP of Software，我们公司最大的一个 leader，之前是汇报给 Bill Dally。对，带着 Deep Image Generation 的团队。我现在 report 给 Dwight。He is the first software engineer in this company.

After I left research, we changed the name. I don't call my team the Imagination Research Team. We call it Cosmos Lab. This is the whole change.

Sora 的遗憾与 OpenAI 的取舍

问： I heard that Sora didn't come out of your team. It makes you regret it, right?

答： It's not a pity, I'm just very happy to be able to make such a big contribution with people I've worked with before. I'm very happy. The regret is that every researcher wants to make a contribution. Seeing this show, this contribution, so big, of course I will feel very happy, but on the one hand, I also feel that what is it? I am a person who likes to reflect on myself. I often try to understand how to make myself better.

Speaking of Sora, I would like to say one more thing.

问： Why do you think OpenAI basically turned off this product line?

答： Sora is a major research job. Of course, it also has many applications. OpenAI is a very ambitious company, and they have a lot of talent. Sam Altman has always been an investor since he was at Y Combinator. He of course wants to have this kind of investor mentality and he hopes that the company has all kinds of projects.

I think in the past year, they have received this Anthropic huge competitive pressure. They saw that Anthropic generated huge economic benefits on Coding Agent. When you are chatting with ChatGPT, the number of tokens you generate is probably the most one minute is generated. Then you do this Coding Agent, you can work 24 hours, 14, 8 hours. This token is very large. They just think this is a good direction. Then, the experience of the company is focused on this. 要做出一个不容易的决定。

为什么 NVIDIA 要做研究？

And designing chips, designing the structure of this computer, its cycle is very long. You can't say I will change it right now.

需要很长的一段时间来做这个规划。所以你要做这方面的研究，做他们投资去理解到什么是可能是重要的问题要解，设计出更好的晶片、更好的 infrastructure 来满足这些 AI 大公司。

我总觉得这世界上如果每个 people with ambitions and ambitions have tools to do what they want to do, this world will be a better world.

On the one hand, I am very happy to see OpenAI, Anthropic, and several major Chinese companies make a breakthrough. We will have young people with ambitions in this society. We also hope they have their chance. We can make these models and share them with them. They can make very good applications, very good extension models, or get inspiration from this to make better models for them. Then everyone's different ideas can be laid.

There are still a lot of things to do, especially in the huge business field. A lot of hardware problems, a lot of business problems need to be solved. I think we give the community a signal that we will help you in this regard. When you see this trend, see our commitment, we do it from generation 1 to generation 2, 2.5 to 3, and so on. You see that we are doing better step by step. So that everyone can expect more.

因为大家会看到这个趋势之后，他就可以把他的资源投在更重要的道果上面，去做出重大的贡献。因为每家公司再有钱的公司，资源都是有限的。那你不找到痛点，找到这个关键点去做投资、做进步的话，你是不容易脱颖而出的。

It's so hard to build a company, and it's so hard to solve problems. I think we should make these models to help them share the pressure. I don't think it's about competition. I think it's about helping everyone succeed.

为什么选择做世界模型而非大语言模型？

问： Why did you set up a very important project at that time and didn't choose the most popular large-scale model at that time? 我不选择一个像 Sora 那样的模型，却选择了一个具身的世界模型？

答： 大规模模型 were very well developed at that time. Then my background is not large-scale models, I was born in computer vision. Born in CV.

这 image, video 拍换。This is the background of the past. I went to this path. Because of my background, the partners who worked with me also have similar backgrounds. So we went this way.

Why didn't we go to the large-scale model? In addition, NVIDIA also has a very strong large-scale model team. I don't think I made much contribution there. I think Nemo is getting better and better. I mainly want to solve some problems here more suitable for me to solve the problem.

When Sora first came out, it was also a "World Simulator", but at that time the main application was more like this creative application. The creation is very interesting, everyone hopes to use better houses to tell stories, to present what they want, that is, to visualize, to help everyone understand the world you see. This is a very good application.

But at that time, we also saw that we are developing very fast in this digital AI. At the same time, there are many social problems that need physical tools. Physical tools that can really change the physical state of the physical world are not enough.

For example, when people are old, they can't drive. But if you can't drive, your quality of life will be much lower. But if you have a car, you can still have mobility when you are older. And then there are a lot of jobs that are very labor-intensive and very dangerous. If you have a robot like this, you can help improve people's lives.

Jensen has very strict requirements for the team. 我们的目标是帮助这些建 solution 的公司成功。有时候会觉得有点像隔靴搔痒，因为你不太了解痛点在哪里。你设计模型的时候，你设计一个产品，如果你不了解你的客户的话，你就没办法最佳化。这就是为什么我会常来中国的原因，就是想理解一下大家遇到的问题是什么，怎么去帮助他们。

Zero Billion Dollar Business

Jensen often talks about his 0 billion dollar business. You can not make money, but when the business is successful, it must be very influential. It's huge. You can't say that you are satisfied with making 100 million a year. This scale is very big for many companies. 但对英伟达的公司而言，这并不是一个 distraction，是个分心。

就是你要去解最重要的问题，产生最大的贡献。然后我们觉得 physicalize 是一个够大的问题，可以产生最大的贡献。所以在带这个方向的时候要很小心，就是要去解最重要的问题，而不是去解一些短暂可以产生成果，但它的影响并不是很大。这是其中一个问题。当然就是要做最好，那这也是很难的。

从量子通讯到计算机视觉的转向

At that time, I wanted to study quantum communication in the United States. Because I think this thing is very mysterious. It is based on quantum communication, you can directly pass the message from A to B.

But before I went to the United States, I stayed in Taiwan for a year with Intel. Then I met a friend. We all studied there. He did this image recognition there. This is my first time to get to know AI. Because I learned about communication before. I saw it in the video, I think it's amazing. It can judge what's inside from these pixels. Who is it? What is the object? I think it's a little bit different from AI and computer vision. I started to have some impressions.

I applied to Maryland University in the United States. I started my PhD there. The earliest computer vision was not a blog. The main funding research was national defense. Maryland is close to Washington, D.C. So, at that time, there were some very powerful people who were doing computer vision AI in the early days.

I was going to study quantum communication when I got to that school. Later, I found out that there was a computer vision there. I started learning AI and computer vision from him.

The first question I asked was to see who the person walking on the platform was from the video. It was a very interesting question. I gradually Transformation and then do this AI and then do these video recognition in the earliest days.

Then later during the post-doc period, I also learned how to use these common understanding directions called Shape Matching and Segmentation AI computer vision. So you have to learn everything. At that time, we did support vector machine. That is a very traditional way of machine learning.

You have to learn some graphical model, energy minimization, and various 3D calibration.

加入 MERL 与深度学习的启蒙

Then my first job was at the MERL (Mitsubishi Electric Research Lab). The research institute is usually free to do research. I have a lot of time to learn. So I learned deep learning there. The journey model is my professor, Rama Chellappa. He believes in the journey model. He believes in patience. He believes that you have to put the depth in this 这是 understanding 的一部分。

所以我在那时候学 deep learning 的时候，也带留意深层的这一块。后来有一年去了 New York City，看到 Ian Goodfellow 的这个 GAN—— 只要能生成 32×32 的女生的脸，然后看起来不像鬼，然后就觉得自己很成功了。

问： 为什么生成是理解的一部分？

答： Richard Feynman 他讲的："If I cannot create, I cannot understand." When you can generate it, you can understand it thoroughly. This person's learning is a bit like it. When you can talk, it means you already understand.

In the early days, computer vision also divided this kind of discriminative model and generative model. Discriminative model is that it actually has no generation ability, but it can judge whether this is A or B. Determination. The generation model is can be used to make a distinction, but it still includes the ability to rebuild this signal, which can be described. When you can describe it clearly, everyone may think that you understand this thing better.

Then it is discriminative and generative. So, like the earliest LSNet, you can do ImageNet classification, we will see it as a discrimination network.

工程思维与研究之路

When you ask the right question, you will find the right direction. Engineering helps you to tell everyone that this is the right question. It's about doing things. Before I went to the United States, I was influenced by engineering. So AI is also an accident for you.

I think it is also because of this reason that the universe will attract so many people to make speeches here.

计算机视觉的"最好之路"

Computer vision. Just go to the best sister. If it's continuous, often encounter such non-convex problems. Is that you can't find the best solution. If it's a good-for-nothing, it's this NP-hard problem. You don't have enough computing power to find the best solution. You still study the algorithm to find an answer. But you don't know how far the answer is from the best solution.

In order to ensure that your answer is not too far from the best solution, just have a certain guarantee and prove that this is called Bound. Maybe this plus is the answer you find is not plus, but it is probably 10% worse than the plus, and I am 20% worse than any other answer.

In order to prove this Bound, many early research will start to make some assumptions. Assumptions make your math cleaner and you can find the answer, but assumptions also make you far from reality.

I was looking for the beauty of math and I was trying to ignore the distance from the real world. After a while, I realized that this is not correct. Because AI itself is an application, intelligence is applied. I like to get closer to the essence of the problem and not be confused by these fancy math.

学会沟通与协作

And then there was another stage, which was related to my background growing up. I was always focused on doing things, instead of focusing on making others understand what you're doing.

After I started doing Invertor, I think my research is pretty good. Before others see these image translations, I made these things. But I don't understand how to express what I made. 嗯，我后来理解到，尤其是开始做大模型的时候，我开始理解到团结合作是非常重要一件事情。人跟人的沟通呢，其实是一个高复杂度的问题。

Assuming you have n people, you and these other n people communicate with n squared. n squared in terms of complexity is a bad complexity, it's just not easy to scale. When there are many people in the group, everyone has to point to the right point, and communication is not easy. It's better to be N, linear, or sub-linear.

I started to know that I had to make some huge contributions. When everyone needs to work together, we must make things very clear so that everyone can understand and everyone's goals can be consistent. I hope everyone can understand what they are doing and can move in the same direction.

大家都在用它，我刚讲马良神笔，我看到用户的反馈让我 [印象深刻]。

SPADE 与 GauGAN 命名故事

We have been researching this direction together. Of course, there are also cooperation with Zhu Junyan and Wang Dingjun. We are studying this topic together. At that time, we developed a algorithm called SPADE, Spatially-Adaptive Denormalization.

After that, I was very happy to do a demo inside the company. Then Jason was very excited to see it. Then he asked me what my name was. I said "Spade" and he didn't like it. It's hard to understand. It's not a user language.

At that time, the paper was finished and I voted for CVPR. But it wasn't put on the archive. Then the company saw it and told me not to put it on the archive. So that Jensen can announce it to everyone at his conference in 2019 at the GTC.

然后我觉得很兴奋，很好的机会。那他们就在想，这叫什么？我们公司有一个 marketing genius，就想说这叫，因为那时候算法都是什么，GAN 什么 GAN 什么 GAN。GAN 的时代。对，GAN 的时代。然后那个他叫做 Greg Estes，然后他就提出叫 GauGAN。He is French, so he took this name out.

Then everyone heard his name, very reasonable painter, famous painter. Then the application was also this painting thing. Then it came out.

At that time, it was originally announced at the GDC, his donation meeting. As a result, he had too many products to introduce that year. I remember I was rehearsing with him on Sunday night. I was going to give a demo on stage. Then I received a notice that there were too many products to be talked about that night. He decided not to put this high-end on his keynote.

It's the same as making a news article. I gave a lot of demos to the media friends to see, but I didn't put it on his conference. After many media friends saw him, it was the most popular work in GTC.

Coupled GAN 与信息瓶颈

Coupled game. It's a combination of two game's production networks. Coupled together, it creates an information bottleneck. All deep learning is about compression information. The bottleneck is to give the network a chance to find the essence.

One game is modeling a distribution. Then you have two GANs to model two distributions. One is code, one is code. When you are coupled together, it has a limit. It will find some commonality. Then it can let you do this conversion from code to code.

The whole generation network is doing distribution modeling. Distribution modeling is that you can sample. It produces an image, a sun, a sea, or a video. But people don't just want to generate. He wants to be able to control the things he generates. Control is to have signals.

There are many types of signals. A common signal is to use the image as a signal. Another way to understand it is that you are drawing. Then there is a segmentation, which is like a painter. What color represents the mountain? What color represents the water? This is a signal.

Then come again, Text to image, text to video. Text and segmentation are different. Segmentation is to give you a specific pixel. It helps you to match it. Text is different. Its structure is different from image structure. It's different from video structure. Because the structure is different, it's harder to learn.

需要更多的数据。所以我在发言过程当中我是理解到这个问题，所以我是从比较容易的方向一步一步往上走。然后容易的最早是这种 segmentation，这种 age 或一个 image。

That's why I said earlier that I was not determined enough to deal with it. Because at that time, I always thought that text-to-image was a very difficult problem. And then I think that there is not enough data and computing power to do this in this field. In fact, there is. Then it is because I didn't do it, so I can't do it.

早期对 LLM 的预判

答： Yes, actually, in the early days, I had a few friends. We participated in NeurIPS every year. We were discussing that there was no GPT at that time. It was early. We were discussing that if there is real AI, it will really breakthrough. What is the first one that will breakthrough?

At that time, I told everyone that it was text. It's language.

答： It should be 16-17.

I know that there are too many miscellaneous words in video. There are many things that are far away from the essence of knowledge. It is more of a world observation. The test is already very pure, relatively close to the symbol. So to produce some similar intelligence performance, the first thing is language.

Although I know that the earliest AI will occur in language, and then it really is like that. But at that time, I just liked this kind of visual signal, so I kept staying here in the depth of this visual signal.

Video-to-Video 与实习生们

问： 后面这几个 GAN 的工作你要不要讲一下？

答： 那时候就是 image translation，从 A 就是马变斑马、风景化变真实的风景，然后后来又开始做 video，然后我们那时候做一个叫 V2V。

And because of this, I became friends with the inventor of the game, Ian Goodfellow. We discussed a lot and luckily, many excellent researchers, such as Yu Jiahui, Tim Brooks, and many others came to my place to intern and I learned from them. I did a lot of work.

这是围绕的，这是 image translation、video translation 这方向走。

拥抱 Scalability：Bitter Lesson 的领悟

When I was studying for my PhD, I was learning about traditional computer vision. After my PhD, I learned about deep learning. I thought that I shouldn't do handcrafted algorithm design, or handcrafted feature engineering, but data-driven.

I realized that a more scalable approach is easier to succeed. So I often tell myself that when you make choices, you should find something more scalable. Later, everyone will say "Bitter Lesson".

When I was making Gain, I was very happy. But I kept thinking: 到底是不是 scalable？因为大家都知道说他很难去训练。所以我担心这东西就是可能最后不 scalable。

那一年余佳慧来我这边实习的时候，我跟他研究的题目就是要去 scale GAN。那时候还很早，那时候我就看到余佳慧他的才华洋溢，然后就是做出很多。就是虽然我们那时候没有写出一个 paper，但那时候做的实验量非常的精准。他的想法我看到，哇，还可以这样想。

然后就是，比如说那时候，说 GAN 是一个 Generator 跟 Discriminator 嘛。那时候我有信的是有很大量的 GPU，一个 Cast 来 train GAN。他就想到说每一个 GPU 都放一个 Discriminator，但是它的 weight 都不一样。所以好像很多人同时跟这个生成式网路做对抗，在那个时代能去实现的东西是很不容易的一件事情。

There was another intern at that time, Jeremy Bernstein. He later invented the Muon Optimizer. Now everyone is using the Muon Optimizer. He came to my lab at that time. I studied with him how to use this algorithm to stabilize the GAN. These two methods failed in the end. But they all developed very amazing and successful work.

Jeremy, from that time on, we have written a series of papers on how to stabilize the training with the early Muon algorithm. He has been going down and developing the Muon algorithm.

Transformer 与 Diffusion 的转折

问： 2021 那时期？2017 年是 Transformer 发明出来了。

答： 对，17 年 Transformer。Transformer 发明出来之后，我必须讲，我不是早期去接触 Transformer 的。

问： 当时的英文还是 LLM？

答： 对，这是 LLM 那一块。我一直在专注在 Gain。然后早期的 Gain 呢，比较好训练的都是用 Convolution Network。

After he brought in the diffusion transformer, the people who did the diffusion started to move towards the transformer. So at that time, from the algorithmic level, I felt that the game was not scalable. Then I told the team that the unscalable thing could not be done in the end. Then I went to diffusion and started to go to diffusion.

This is a major transformation period. Diffusion was initially an image, then it became a multi-view image. Multi-view image became 3D generation. We did a series of work on this aspect, which is the Edify series. Edify image generator, Edify 3D, Edify video, and then do the production of each layer using Diffusion.

研究员的心态与本质追求

问： In the long exploration process of CV, there have been several changes in the mathematical formula, from traditional to GAN and then to diffusion. What kind of mentality should a researcher have when he is doing a transformation?

答： 传统的科研一样就是把事情越就找到真正找到本质，找到最简单的方式去描述这个物世界是怎么运作的。我觉得现在的方法就是把事情越变越简单。

然后在 Cosmo 这边，我们也是从数个模型，最后变成了现在这个 Cosmo 3 的一个模型。也同意了。对，就是接着理解到 OK，原来这就是事情的本质。

然后每一个方向，我都是花了五到十年在投入啊。我觉得未来的决定，It's very helpful for me to understand a lot of things now.

关于实习生与年轻人的启发

I also found that you mentioned your intern several times. In AI Lab, is it common for interns to use ideas? How do you see young people?

"The degree of economic advantage is based on how much money is left in one person's pocket. The degree of research advantage should be based on how much ideas are left in another person's head."

If you are just a colleague in the industry, the diversity of ideas is low. Because we have a lot of interns here, we can collaborate with these people with different backgrounds, research and learn from each other. I think this is something that helps me grow and also helps them grow. It's a very important development.

加入 NVIDIA 的选择

问： You joined MERL in 2012 after graduating from university. Then you joined NVIDIA in 2016. How did the professional change happen? How did you join NVIDIA?

答： Since I started doing deep learning, I have been very confident in my computing power. In MERL, it is not a company that values computing power, but a company that values computing. At that time, in order to do research, do good research, I often talked to my manager at that time, 要求要买 GPU。开会就是说我们需要 GPU 要做这件事情。

在那个三菱电机有一个 long term mentor，他叫昂州执照，他也是一个很有名的研究员。然后他那时候就决定离职加入苹果做自动车。然后我突然间觉得说，就是当初把我留在三菱电机的主要原因走了。然后我就开始思考说我是不是也要换工作？

So I naturally switched jobs and went to Weibo to chat with these big companies. At that time, everyone saw Google, Apple, Amazon, these big companies in the meta. Then their recruiter found me. Then I saw NVIDIA. Yes, I always wanted to buy their GPU. Then I was so short of GPUs, so I wanted GPUs. Why don't I join a company that produces GPUs? So at that time, I decided to join NVIDIA.

我父母不理解，because it was a company that I had never heard of before. I didn't know it at that time. They said Apple is good, Google is good, why do you want to join NVIDIA? I said that because I think GPU is the most important.

Especially when I started doing couple games, it was an unsupervised approach. So the unsupervised approach means that the data is more easily obtained. You don't need a tag. I thought the most important thing was to calculate the profit and the data. Since I didn't need to do that, I went to a place that had profit and loss.

有一个 interesting thing is that I later realized that the manager of MERL, when I argued with him about GPUs, as long as I won, he would give me some money to buy GPUs. At the same time, he would buy NVIDIA's stock. Then he retired.

问： 它还没有告诉你什么当时？

答： 它后来跟我说了。当时没有告诉你，不然你也可以买了。是的。

早期 NVIDIA Research 的印象

问： I saw you were already working with NVIDIA people on some papers when you were at MERL, right?

世界模型的定义之争

问： Today, everyone's definition of world models is still very unclear. Can you tell us about your definition of world models?

答： I am a very practical person. Why would people design a model? It can be used, and there are many ways to use it.

For example, you design a model to describe this world. With this model, you can predict what will happen next. So its purpose is to predict. This is a kind of world model. Why design a world model? Use and prediction.

The other kind is that you want to understand why this thing happened. In some ways, the whole of physics is to build a world model. To understand how this world works. From Newton's theorem to quantum theorem, we need to understand how the world works. We need to build a model to help us understand how it works.

Of course, from deep learning, we need to teach this understanding, which is to use some standard data to teach this model. How this thing works is because of this thing. Then, using a lot of data to make a plan to help the future new world. When it happens, you can use this to open the video signal and then explain it to help people understand what happened.

For example, this factory is in the factory. Why is this place suddenly stuck? Then it may be that some workers forgot to open something before. It is also a purpose of this world model to understand what happened. Find the problem.

There is another kind of world model to reconstruct this three-dimensional world. Reconstructing this three-dimensional world has great uses. You can plan how your things will go along the way, and then you can just let people experience it. Although you are not born in this real world, you can travel in this world in a virtual state.

After all, we are in the same world. These models are different is to describe the same thing through different observations. Reconstruction is a very important study. I used to do reconstruction, but now I am no longer doing reconstruction. I am mainly doing the understanding of the physical world and the production of the physical world.

Right, these things are prediction. Everyone will have different interpretations of the world model. 经过这么多年，还是没有一个共同的定义。然后我认为去定义 World Model 很可能会走向同样的道路。我觉得可能不是很重要的一件事情。

Why is LLM a relatively accurate word? LLM is Large Language Model. It has a large model and it's a language. Why is this word a consistent and accurate definition? But the world model has been controversial.

LLM is Large Language Model. Language model can predict what words will happen next. Large means that its model is very large. This is very clear. World model is a tool that can help you model the world. Then you model the world as a tool, 你要做什么用途呢？因为用途不同，所以你 model 的世界方式不一样。所以当只要你对这个世界这个模型有不同的用途之后，就有不同的定义。

答： 就是第一代，这个是去年的工作。这个步调很快。那时候开始做 Cosmos 的时候，我强调一个点就是我们要迭代快速。那时候深受 DeepSeek 的影响。 因为 DeepSeek is an amazing company. It can be folded three times a year to produce DeepSeek v3.

So I always emphasize that we have to fold fast. Folding fast means that we can keep improving. Better than before. But the topic we challenged at that time was physical world modeling. At that time, in fact, it was not very clear in the 20 years. Everyone was still in the process of finding out what kind of world modeling would be helpful to everyone.

What I just said is that it is not surprising that using world modeling, 怎么用它？Prediction 或是 Understanding？那就是做这种 Video Model 来帮助 Predict Future，然后或是做这种 Recent Model 来解释发生什么事情。

At the beginning, we worked with some partners to understand their needs. We had some ideas and then made some models. After working with these partners, we slowly learned from them. 跟真实世界的讯号一定有差距。可不可以用模型来帮助它更逼真？那就说 transfer。我解释发生什么事情就说 reason。当时是三个。

对，后来理解到说我如果可以去描述这个 pixel 是被这个 pixel 是怎么变化的—— The pixel change is very close to the action change. So we made a Cosmos Policy model.

LV 门店的启示：从 22 个模型到 1 个模型

Then I discovered that this is the same world. No matter where you look at it, your model is the same world. You model is learning an internal representation of the world.

Another thing is that the core concept of the Foundation Model is that it can be integrated into hundreds of thousands of generations. It can learn from various data to learn the model of this model. So if you can put the data you used in the recent, the data used in the trend pretty, the data used in the trend spread, the data used in the trend policy, and the data used in the trend policy all together, you are the model with a higher upper limit.

There is another one in the middle. It is a kind of intellectual problem. I remember when I first built this. I was trying to figure out the model for the first version of Cosmos. I wanted to help others with the model. I was working with partners. I needed models A, B, C, D, E, F, G. I was trying to figure out the model. I needed 22 models.

I had a meeting with Jensen. I told him that I expected to need 22 models. When Jensen heard it, he thought I was working very hard. He said, "Very good. We're very hard." He said:

"But do you know Louis Vuitton LV store? When it reduces its goods, after the number of goods in the shelf is increased, you don't want too many things to confuse your consumer, let him not be able to make decisions."

That has a great impact on me. I understand that I have encountered problems myself. Because I know clearly that I want to use A or B, the others are more unclear. Then again, the difficulties in execution. Every model you come out, we don't just send a paper and end it. We have to help the user use it.

As long as every model comes out, we have to maintain it and solve the problem. Then when you have several models, it's hard to get more and more chips. Then it affects the speed of your delivery.

所以决定要做这个 Omni Model 的 World Model，就是 Cosmos 3。就数个方向：第一个是描述同一个世界，所以其实是可以合在一起的。然后第二个 Foundation Model 就是吸收各式各样的 β 合在一起。and it's much simpler in development. So it's the way to go to Cosmos 3.

问： So 2 to 3 is actually a big change.

答： Yes, the change from 1 to 2 is the improvement of data. And there were some changes when I put the power on at 2. But I think 2 to 3 is a big gap.

问： How long did 3 take?

答： I started doing it in October last year. It happened to be after the 2nd. Yes, actually, at that time, I knew I had to do 3rd in a earlier period. But at that time, I had already started 2.5. I completed 2.5. I completed 2.5 and then started doing 3rd. So maybe 3rd was... I started to know I had to do 3rd in September. Then I actually started in October and November. and it's been almost half a year. More than half a year.

Cosmos 3 的技术架构与开源承诺

问： A Chinese entrepreneur who works on world models, he said he read the Cosmos 3 paper for a week. And he reads it every day. He thinks that Cosmos 3 is a great innovation in technology.

答： Someone mentioned it before Mitchell Transformer, and someone mentioned it before Parse Model. We are the first to scale Mitchell Transformer to such a large model, and put audio, video, and action together.

这些东西从概念上来讲就是东西合在一起，但你真正要把它做出来不是那么容易。那真正做出来就是这些细节。所有的这些大圆模型都是 Transformer 架构 —— you can say that everyone is not innovative, but its details will make this certain model much better than other models.

I think that after so many years, I will pay more attention to the effect that this thing can produce. I often don't pay attention to these things. Is it a revolutionary original? Yes, I think it's useful to generate impact. It's important to solve problems.

We hope to help the open source community, that is, to do open source modeling to help the entire physical AI. What we have seen in recent years is that these frontier labs are heading towards the B source. 即使写 paper 也不愿意讲出那些关键的环节。

We decided to walk a different road. We say what can be said as much as possible, we make things very clear. Then we open source this model, and we also open source the framework of how we train this model.

答： It's not really related. DeepSeek's work has a very deep impact on AI. First, it opened a company called Mitchell & Esper. And you can see that its recent model has forced this to the extreme.

I hope I can help this physical eye to arrive in the world faster.

为什么把 Language / Video / Action 放到同一模型

问： 你们在这次为什么选择首先在输入层同时能够输入语言、video、audio 和 action？这是一个重要的决策吗？

答： 我觉得这个世界不是只有视觉，对吧？然后也有听觉。但我也想加入触觉。但触觉的讯号还不好。touch sensor 这些东西还觉得还在快速迭代当中。

问： 这个需要灵巧手？

答： 对，需要灵巧手，需要数据。

那我觉得大模型基本上思路有两个：一个是让 language 当成 first class citizen，像 coding，像 chat；另外一种是让视觉讯号，video 当成是 first class citizen，像 cadence，像 reel。我们认为 The most different between the physical world model and the digital world model is that the physical world agent will take action and change the state of the world. We think that a good physical world foundation model also needs to take action as a first-class citizen.

This is why we put language, video, and action together to build this Cosmos.

I remember Yang Zhilin told me that they use language modeling as the most important tool for improving their intelligence. Language can bring in human knowledge and help humans communicate with physical AI. Video is a lot of visual information, and audio is a lot of listening information to describe how the world works. Using video is more efficient in capturing the physical operation of the world. It's hard to use language.

但是人跟这个模型，这个模型之后建出来是要服务人的嘛。它不懂 language，你是没办法跟它沟通的。然后这个模型最后是要帮助这些 machine to take action 的，所以它不懂 action，它是没办法去改变这个世界的。

我的目标不是去追求 AGI。AGI 本身也很难去定义嘛。语言是发展适合人类的，但你不知道机器是不是接受这一套。也许你就从视觉讯号里面直接去学这个世界的怎么运作，得到一个 intelligent，然后发展出另外一个文明。那你从这个角度看，也许语言讯号是一种干扰。

多模态融合的原理

问： Is it beneficial to integrate all the models or is it just a limitation?

答： In the past year or even a year, we have been studying the integration of these models. We got some clues from various studies. We connected them together in the Cosmos 3.

For example, in the Cosmos Policy work, we found that Video and action together is to help action. When you are directly predicting action, we found that in addition to predicting what action you want to do, you also predict the next state that will occur after taking this action. This observation helps you do the training. So we know that the video is to help action.

Sound can also help audio, sound can also help video generation. When you know "Kak" a sound, you will know the time of contact is that point. So you know this is mutual.

Then, people who do video know that from text to video, this is a process of increasing the amount of information. 讯息量变大代表说有很多种可能性。很多种可能性的方式是比较难去学习的。就是一种东西可能有十种可能，那这东西就没有固定的目标不好学。

So when you are making a video or image, everyone will notice that when your text description is very detailed, it is easier to produce a good video. So you can know that the detailed description of text can also be used in this video.

Then we do this Cosmos 3, just like putting these Cosmo Reason, Cosmo Predict, Cosmo Transfer, Cosmo Path together. It has its own benefits to be combined. The whole thing is simplified.

双塔架构与设计取舍

问： 你们采用了双塔设计——一个塔在处理离散信息，另一个在处理连续信息。为什么？

答： There are many reasons. At the beginning, Cosmo's reason was Discrete, which started from the Vision Language model. The Predict, Transfer, and Part are continuous. So, we know the work for understanding of design. We know the work for generation. Put them together is a reasonable choice at this stage.

Then there are many ways to use Cosmo. But the most common is to do post-training. Maybe use your video action to train the generator, or you just want to use the reason. Just use your own domain to train these understanding data.

When you have two of them together, you can cut the influence of the rule. It is for the customer to use. If we all connect together, that is, generation and understanding together, I am going to change this generation distribution now. In the process of changing, because they are all linked together, your data will also change the performance of your understanding side.

If you don't have two sets and you are one, then the understanding side, since you want to change, then your data does not have understanding data. It is easy for this understanding part to disappear. It is not convenient for customers to use it. So dividing into two is helpful for use. Although it is relatively not elegant enough.

Because you still have to pre-decide its structure. The whole deep learning is to let the data decide what to say, rather than you doing the distinction. But at this stage, I think this is more reasonable and suitable for everyone to use.

Speaking of this, you can guess that our next goal is simpler. Why do we need two sets? One set is enough. But when we move forward with one set of goals, we have to consider 这些使用者是不是容易用上它？

因为我们的目标是帮助大家赢，而不是自己产生一个可以做很多事情的模型。我们相信机器人每个都不太一样，有个相机的数量、相机的位置，然后自动车，每个都不太一样，我们觉得需要克制。

关于"泛化"是核心问题

问： 一位研究员问你，你现在把所有模型合到一个里，那理论上它也可以做 coding，也可以驱动机器人。它有没有可能在单一维度上（例如 coding）比 Claude 更强？

答： 我还是喜欢讲的《孙子兵法》。如果你想什么都好，你就必须在训练过程中博学多闻，触碰很多不同的类别，让你提升你的知识水平。

当你确定你只需要用这个单一的 application 的时候，是不是有些调整是——因为你不 care 其他东西了——有没有东西是你愿意放弃，然后就是做比较好。因为如果你什么都不愿意放弃的话，你就会打得很辛苦。我觉得策略往往就是，[要有取舍]。

We also know that if you can pass the generator's gradient back to the recent one, it can help your recent one to do better representation learning. But in this paper, it takes time. We didn't do all the experiments we wanted to do.

问： As far as I know, everyone is discussing it, and some partners and some classmates have given pretty good feedback.

答： Formation is a core problem, the core problem of any AI. In the AI of the physical world, I think one of the things we need to achieve is to form.

Suppose I teach the robot today that I like to fold my clothes like this. I will show this robot how I do it once or twice. Can he learn quickly in real life? Learn this thing quickly, and then read the instruction manual for this physical guy. He knows how to operate this machine, how to do that test in this factory. I think these are very important capabilities that are achieved by physical adders.

I want to say that in the foundation model part, what can we do to help these physical adder developers? So we may improve the middle one towards these. Improve these capabilities of the emulation. To add these things to the Cosmo model.

问： For example, what specific optimization do you have for this?

答： The optimization is like accelerating. It will definitely happen. We hope that this model can run faster and faster. Then, some other optimization is the optimization of ability and optimization of translation. Yes, this thing may change some of the structures or some training objectives. Or use some special curated data to do this training. It's not very clear, it needs to be tested.

问： 它是一个实验科学。

答： 对，是实验科学。就是我常常觉得 deep learning 就很像中医一样，就是试出来的。对，然后在试的过程当中，你做详细的实验记录，从里面去理解中间的法则。

关于 Language 是否应更强

问： Some researchers also suggested that the language rendering of this model can increase its scale a little bit. Because they still think that LLM is the key to improving intelligence. Do you agree?

答： I think in the early image generation research, including Google's image generation, it was mentioned that the stronger your language understanding, the stronger your image generation ability is with a larger T5 model.

I believe that you should use a larger semantic representation to help. I agree. After all, the application of Physical AI is different from the coding or chat that we often talk about. So it still needs to be verified.

What I want to do is to understand the real pain points. Then find a suitable way to strengthen the model ability from this pain point. Some signals that everyone gets, better models, when you have no resources, you should put them in. But the more challenging thing is how to do the trend when you have limited resources.

So maybe for the common sense, intelligence may not be the most critical variable. Do you need your robot to solve the problem of the number of hours? 你需要你的机器人会解 coding 的问题吗？我觉得你可能更关注他能不能把你的工厂要组装的东西做好，或家庭的卫生这些操作把它做好。

Physical AI 与 Agentic AI

问： 现有的这些 for agent 的模型是一样的吗？

答： 这是我一直在思考的问题。

Because there are several model projects, we mainly divide them into two categories. One is called Agentic AI, which is to do coding chat, and then go to Agentic. In this, we have this Nemotron model, which is the Nemotron 3 Ultra that this team has recently released.

In the physical AI, the model is mainly COSMO. COSMO is a base model. NVIDIA is also very concerned about automobiles, machines, and factories. For us, these are all the applications of physical AI. In the automotive industry, we call it Apollo Mario's effort. It is a model that is made on COSMO. 特殊版本古物词是在 Cosmo 上面做对机器人相关的用法，还包含这些 Hobody Control 的这些东西。

我是把这些做自动车内部、做自动车、做机器人这些看成是也是我的客户，然后也希望帮助他们成功。然后在 PhysicalAI 这边就是 Cosmo 为核心来去辅助这些主要的 Downstream 的开发者可以获得成功。

问： How big will physical AI be in your opinion?

答： This should be a huge market. I'm not sure if this is my specialty. But as the population ages, as the demand for self-sufficiency in the manufacturing industry grows, we think this will be a huge market.

评测与数据的挑战

问： Because there are now few effective evaluation methods for world models. Do you have any good explorations?

答： World model, large-scale model, everyone is pursuing better evaluation and testing methods.

In general, there are three steps in the model evaluation: 1. Benchmark — 有一些固定的 dataset，你去上面量测它的跨体 2. Arena style — 就是 A 跟 B 比，看谁比较好 3. 跟着 ASPR — 去真正有这个痛点的人，去解这个问题

那我觉得这三个都很重要。在 PhysicalAI 里面，第三个特别重要。因为每个 coding agent，大家都在解 coding 的问题，digital use 的问题。But each of the physical problems is different.

问： Data is also a difficulty. How did you do this?

答： Data is a difficult thing, especially in physical AI. Because every type of physical AI is different.

There are two types of physical data: 1. Navigation data — from A to B, easier to do 2. Manipulation data — how to use that hand or tool to operate to complete a set goal

The operation side is more complicated. We found a trend that everyone is increasingly pursuing this kind of machine arm that is close to the human hand. Then the point of view is that this world, the world of human beings, is built for human use, so most of the tools are suitable for human hands to operate.

AI requires a lot of data. The more data you have, the faster you can get breakthroughs. So most data collectors are human beings. So today we see everyone moving towards the human hand.

So when we are in this Cosmos 3, we also specifically add this data from the Egocentric perspective, including how the human eye sees this thing, how the human hand operates this object from the low human side.

Cosmos 3 的满意与遗憾

问： What is the thing that makes you very satisfied with this model? And what is the thing that makes you a little regretful?

答： The thing that makes me satisfied is that I told everyone that I could put all the past models together and do better than all the previous models. This thing happened. Our current model is better than the individual model in the past. I was very happy.

The second thing is that this is our first time to build a model with several models. Now we are building a model together. I am very proud of this thing to happen.

What is the regret? I think our model is very good. Because of time limitations, I think the model can still be improved. But because of time limitations, we can't fully train it. So we have to cancel it. There are still many places that we want to change, but we didn't have time to change them before.

The advantage is that we will continue to do 3.1 and 3.2, and we will fill in the things we didn't do before.

问： Have you ever thought about what it would be like to be the 97th generation like Huang said?

答： When I heard the 97th generation, my understanding was that we have the determination to keep doing it all the way. And this is a great commitment because this model is very resource-intensive. And then it shows its determination to go down. I have the confidence that this thing will keep going down. The world model is finally approaching this world.

Nemotron 与 Cosmos：两个技术方向

Some layers are traditional transformers, while others are mamba-style, which are close to the RNN structure. This structure has its advantages, because the RNN calculation is cheaper than the transformer in influence. Then, there is a bunch of tokens to be produced by the agent. Sometimes you have to do things for a long time by the agent, so this is the demand for the calculation cost.

Physical AI's structure is not following this path. We are still following the traditional Transformers. But we found the Mitchell Transformers and added Ashen. So the development of the two models is gradually different. When we work closely with our two teams, you can find that many authors from Nemo came from the paper of Cosmo 3.

问： Will these two models be able to become a bigger model in the future?

答： It's possible. Our decision is very simple. How can we best help our clients? That's what we say. We are very low-eagle.

组织架构与 200+ 人协同

问： You mentioned that Cosmos is a very large team. What do you think is the difficulty of working with such a large team?

答： I think there are more than 290 people in the paper, less than 300 people, right? Yes, this team is very large.

Then I see it this way. This is a difficult body of organizational structure. You want everyone to have the same goal, but you also want everyone to be able to make decisions independently.

When everyone's goals are the same, but everyone can't make decisions, the progress will be slow. Because only a small number of decision-makers can make decisions. If I can make the decision, if I can decide how to adjust the data, if I can decide how to do this structure, then our model will not succeed. Because my knowledge is limited, my time is limited, and what we need is that everyone can make important decisions for the organization and development of this model.

The second thing is that if everyone can make decisions, but everyone's goals are not the same, I just want to do Ashen well, I don't care how the video is. Then it may produce different structures, and then it may have a more advanced behavior of the race code.

I think running such a big project is important to make everyone's goals the same, but everyone can make decisions. Then this is on the organizational structure. I spent a lot of effort to design some team operations. This collaboration method makes information transparent. Let everyone have enough confidence to make the right decision for the team.

Of course, we also provide a space for error. Because when a person is afraid of making a mistake, he won't make a decision. So you have to let them make decisions but also accept some decisions as mistakes. But when you make a mistake, you have to be able to fix it quickly.

问： 怎么让 200 多个人都同时做决定啊？这个好难啊。

答： 大家都清楚整个关键，整个 project 之后要达到目标是什么。你要一直去 draw the future clearly and tell everyone. Before the Cosmo 3 paper came out or finished, I told the main leaders and most of the teams that the model we made was like this. Is it completely like this? Maybe 90% similar, 10% different, but when everyone sees the same vision, it is relatively easy to focus.

Like you are a basketball player, you are [going for the same goal].

问： What management methods have you designed to make everyone's information more transparent and better cooperating?

答： 每周？应该超过十次。跟主要的 lead。每个，比如说我们做 video 的，就是定期开会的，一周两三次吧。然后做 understanding 也是定期，就是一周两三次。然后还有各个环节的就是两三次。

There are quite a lot of meetings, and we can have some communication. Of course, in meetings, people will think that meetings are very inefficient. We try to do things to make each meeting more engaging, and then let everyone participate.

你可以一直开会，什么都不做只是讲，也不会成功。你就要选一个均衡。

问： 你看，贵股现在大家说 OpenAI 的企业文化是自下而上，Anthropic 是自上而下，你们属于哪一种？

Physical AI 的 ChatGPT Moment 何时到来

问： When do you think this market will bring about a so-called "ChatGPT Moment"?

答： Everyone is pursuing the "ChatGPT Moment" of physical AI. What is "ChatGPT Moment"? What is the difference between "ChatGPT Moment" and "GPT Moment"? "GPT Moment" is when we say that things can scale. After scaling, the machine will be stronger.

I hope to see the changeability moment as soon as possible. I don't know about this year or next year, but I think it will happen.

问： Do you think human-based robots will become the mainstream in this track?

答： I think the advantage of human-based robots is that they can use a large number of people's data to learn materials to improve these effects. But human-based robots are more like people with legs and hands. Then these things are relatively more complex.

Then many people are doing wheeled. Only the upper and lower layers are human, but the lower layers are a kind of mobile platform. Such a platform can also solve many problems.

都在那个尝试当中。我觉得最终最终可能就是全人形式，所以适合各式各样的操作，因为人类这个环境就是设计给全人形的。但最后还是要关键还是营运成本。

DeepMind's Tanjie has a prediction. He thinks that from 2035 to 2036, human-like robots will become mainstream. I hope it will be earlier. But I'm not sure.

Matrix 觉醒？关于 AI 觉醒的哲学观

问： You said you want to build a black empire for robots. The black empire is a human-made robot with a battery that lives in a virtual world, Matrix. A awakened person tries to break free from the system and end the cycle. You are building this Matrix for robots. What if a robot wakes up and wants to break free from this virtual world?

答： I use Hegel to help everyone think about how to speed up learning with a world model. Many people worry that AI will take over the world when it is too powerful. It will eliminate us. I think this society is built by people. These technologies are still being operated behind the scenes.

I think as long as everyone has a consensus, I think this matter is 会发生。

这比较哲学一点的我觉得—— Pain and suffering are key factors that drive people to make progress. I'm not sure if the intelligence made by silicon has the same pain and suffering. I feel like I'm in a state of pure will.

Of course, I know that we hope this technology can greatly improve human life. We also need to make these corresponding to ensure that it won't affect the development of the normal world.

关于其它"世界模型"团队

问： Speaking of world models, other teams that make world models will treat you as a competitor because everyone thinks that you are also a world model. But you keep saying that I am not your competitor, right? What do you want to say to them?

答： If you can work with us and use what we do, you can go further and faster. Isn't that a good thing? We are all in an open state. If you use us to make a model that is better than us, this model is also open to everyone. We are also helping the entire VQI system. So you do better than us. We also think this is a good thing.

I think working together to solve the problems is also a very worthwhile thing to do. Of course, the other party is to resist each other, set high bar, and then climb up. That is also a very important loop.

They will definitely say that because you want to sell my card again. Why not? 最重要的是你的货币是多少，而不是像这些 Cloud Company，它买了大量的 GPU，但它赚了更多的钱，对吧？

下一个 CUDA 是什么？

问： 你们内部会讨论什么是下一个 CUDA 吗？

答： 有可能是 Cosmos。过去的软体是建于逻辑，然后 CUDA 是帮助把这些 application 所需要逻辑转换成 GPU 的运算。The future software is the core of AI. AI is built on top of other AI. So we think that the Nemo and Cosmos we're building may be the future CUDA.

问： 你觉得 CUDA 会成功的关键要素是什么？

答： I think the idea of CUDA was very promising when it was first proposed. It's a very adventurous idea. So when we weren't sure if this Aster Computing would be a big thing, our company made such a brave investment. The big models we made 得惠于 CUDA 然后可以往下走。

我不会把这个 Cosmo 或 Nemo 闯跟 CUDA 做同等的连结。因为我觉得现在的整个发展已经相对复杂很多。有很多个不同的整个产业是很多个 stack 的合在一起的。我觉得合在一起可能是新的 CUDA，而不会说这个模型单一就是一个 CUDA。

You still need to do serving, you still need to do these infrastructure, there are a lot of things to be put together.

问： What elements do you think CUDA has achieved its success?

答： CUDA was looking for applications at the beginning, scientific computing at the beginning. 后来在 deep learning 出来之后找到 CUDA 最重要的 application 往下走。CUDA 还是一直在提供不同各式各样的 application。

我觉得复制 CUDA 是一个很好的想法，但我不觉得你按照原来的路线就会走一样的路。我觉得这个环境是不一样的。我觉得是要 adaptive，看清楚哪个时间可以做出哪些重要的贡献。

你不会去拿这个锤子去找钉子敲，对吧？ You'll take it and say, "I want to make the next CUDA." That was a very successful decision back then. And now I'm making today's decision.

见证 NVIDIA 从无人识 AI 到 AI 代言人

问： Because you've just joined NVIDIA for 10 years. Have you changed a lot in these 10 years? How many times have you increased your share of NVIDIA?

答： 这些一切都是没有预期到的。这段时间里面我们见证到一个没有人把 AI 跟英伟达连结在一起，变到一个全世界都把英伟达跟 AI 连结在一起。到一个我父母亲不知道什么叫英伟达，到全世界都不知道什么叫英伟达的这个事件。这是很巨大的变化。

中间的历程 It wasn't easy. The company was in a bad shape from the stock price point of view. I remember that the company's stock price dropped a lot when TPU first came out. Some of my classmates had different ideas and examples about the company's future. AMD has been winning TPUs in LPerf every year, and then it has a better price. Then only we participate in the competition.

These things are all hard to predict. In the long run, I have understood what it means to slowly advance and find a goal that you believe in. Very first principle, step by step.

加入 NVIDIA 时的 offer 选择

问： 你加入英伟达的时候，还有哪些 offer？

答： 做科研重要的工具，我要去一个 GPU 众多的地方。那不如去一个生产 GPU 的地方。

另外一个 offer 是谁呀，老师？我有数个 offer，其中有一个投资公司。它跟我讲说，不管我去哪里，不管对方给我多少钱，我都给你四倍。然后希望你可以加入他们的公司，可以一起去研究怎么去用 deep learning 来说投资。

I wasn't interested in this thing. I still wanted to do research and chose NVIDIA. At that time, NVIDIA was probably the less well-known one, right?

Jensen 十年前后的变化

问： Do you think the old Huang of 2016 and the current old Huang have changed a lot?

答： My hair is all white. I think the pressure he took. But he still cares about employees and reads the top five emails of employees in the company very carefully. Then find some signals to help the company move forward.

There is a big change in the size of the company. When we all joined, the company may not be less than 20,000 people. 然后现在已经两倍以上，可能更多。那个就是那时候 GPU 都还是桌机，然后现在都是 Data Center。然后那时候没有 Physical AI，现在 Physical AI 都成为了一个重点。变化是很大的。

问： 你在过程中有见证英伟达的哪些 Pain and Suffering？

答： [Jensen] 先生常常在嘴边讲，他说当然不是真的，他每天都觉得公司只剩下 30 天的现金流，30 天后就要破产，现在还这么说。每次开会都是这样提醒自己、吓唬高管，只是要求自己做出对公司最正确的决定。

然后有一年 pandemic 的时候，整个经济状况不好。At that time, many companies started to disband. I remember at the company meeting, we decided to step on travel. The employees didn't need to travel. Everything was online. So we saved a lot of money.

We were studying what tools we could use. For example, in Silicon Valley, many companies use Slack. We are considering whether to stop using Slack. Anyway, we have email. And we have two or three clouds. For example, we sometimes use Microsoft, sometimes use Google. Can we cancel one? It can save money.

Some companies will reduce the staff expenses by hiring. What NVIDIA is thinking is how to save some unnecessary expenses to take care of employees and go through difficult times together.

NVIDIA 从不裁员的文化

问： Why does NVIDIA keep insisting on not hiring?

答： During the time I was in NVIDIA, I didn't hear any news of hiring. There is no last-ditch elimination, right? Performance review. and let you go.

We think trust between people is very important. When an employee has a sense of recognition and security towards the company, he is willing to say something that is not easy to say in places where people are usually worried about being eliminated.

问： What are the advantages and disadvantages of this type of management model?

答： I think the employees are willing to speak the truth and to work together.

The disadvantage is that when the technology is gradually becoming mature, 这些员工需要一点时间学习新的东西做转型。重新学习新的东西是需要多一点时间的。如果你直接 layoff 再 hire 新的一批人，你可能可以直接 hire 到一些已经会这些东西的人。所以这些经由转型做起来是会比较慢一点。但是你得到的就是员工的信任，然后也可以团结合作的员工。

问： How do you improve the organizational efficiency? Is this a problem for you?

答： As long as everyone is enthusiastic and thinks that what they do is meaningful, then the overall efficiency will improve. Everyone has a choice and will want to do something that they are successful in. If the company can provide this environment for everyone to play, then the efficiency will improve.

长期主义与"跑马拉松"

问： 老黄这种选择是有他的理由的？

答： long-term business. I think for so many years, he has been in the ancient times, and he has seen so many ups and downs. He must have his reasons for choosing this thing. I don't think it's a random choice, it's a thought process. I think this thing is the corporate culture he wants.

问： 是不是说当新科技来的时候，因为答案不会是最快的一个，而是取决于早期 10 年或早期 5 年的早期发展，所以它不是高需求于快？

答： The NVIDIA 是 running marathon, and then look far, and then look at CUDA, which is such a case, 10 years of development, right? So you have to have a strong eye and long-term investment.

问： 你们不 race，是吧？

答： We don't like to fight because we usually do this. You take this mission, we believe you. But we give you a very high bar, hope you can complete it. In old Chinese, it means to accept pain and suffering, torture you to greatness, believe you, and give you [space to grow].

I think this is the most important thing that we haven't understood at the beginning. In order to do things right, and when things go wrong, we have to slowly improve things.

I think this is the part where, since GPT, AI entrepreneurs are under a lot of pressure. During this time, the speed of the delivery, everyone is under a lot of pressure. I think it's pain and suffering. Especially when you're spilling the GPU resources every day, spilling the time of these young people, and the results are not as good as you like.

答： 我大概是四点到五点起来。

嗯，对因为整个整个产业的迭代速度，所以生活步调都变快了。然后还是要学东西还是很多，但是处理的事情又变更多。

问： 你几点睡啊？

答： 我大概大概 10 点左右吧。10 点左右 10 点到 11 点左右。

问： 4 点 5 点起，对哦对。

Mission is the Boss

Apple might be the opposite. We pursue information transparency. This is also a very different culture. Those old-fashioned stories are sometimes more detailed. But many of them are what you can feel when you work at NVIDIA. He knows a lot of employees.

We often say that "Mission is the boss." NVIDIA 有时候像一个有机体。没有那么强的框架。当我们公司今天要走向这个方向的时候，在各种不同组织的团队，但有相对的技能，就会自动 align，就往那个方向前进。就是像一个活的组织，不是一个固定框架。

Mission is the boss，而不是你的 boss，是你的 boss，这几个是最具有特色的。

那这个 Top 5 让公司各个地方的微小讯号都可以传到 [领导层]。

人多的沟通成本与团队多元性

人多的时候就有一个沟通的成本，沟通成本就是负面的。你等于就是要人跟人合作，给产生正相关，但是又要 to reduce the cost of the public.

A group of smart people working together, of course, everyone is very smart, and they understand quickly, and they are quick-witted. But if there is no interaction between people, it is also difficult to reach a 1+1+2. Everyone is prepared to show the best side of the other person, or to show that I am smart with you. This is not necessarily a good state.

我觉得就像打游戏一样，你不要整个团队全部都是弓箭手。可能要有些人是负责防御，有些人是会是执着补血的。各项不同的属性合在一起。这样多元是一个比较好的状态。

Low Ego 是英伟达学来的？

问： 你看今天说了很多你没有竞争对手，然后你不和任何人竞争，都是客户，然后大家都是合作伙伴。这种 low ego 的状态是在英伟达发生的变化吗？

答： 是。Is this really low ego or is it just a kind of hiding? I think it's a kind of confidence. I think what we do can help everyone. My goal is to help everyone do well. But I have a high requirement for what I do. I want it to be good. But my goal is not to defeat my opponent. My goal is 做出好成绩，提出更好的 foundation，让大家可以懂得更快。

问： 这是跟老黄学的吗？

答： 对，我受到影响非常深。

问： 是什么时候学的？

答： 如果你是一个研究员，你毕业的方法就是让你的论文在顶级的会议上被接受，然后 reviewer 都会 question 你的东西是不是 still the art. If you want to "steal" VR, it means you want to defeat all the people. So, researchers all have this mentality that my things are better than yours.

So, following this trajectory, I was a highly competitive individual at the beginning. My things are better than yours. This is my requirement, of course. I hope things will get better and better. But after a while, you know, you always "steal" VR. In a period of time, the next one.

I hope to train new generation talents and help them grow. And then I'm playing the role of NVIDIA ecosystem. I hope the company can gradually feel the benefits. Sometimes I see my friends telling me that after using the model, I have improved the efficiency a lot. I'm very happy. I think my contribution, the hard work of the whole team.

Take Care of Others 是真的吗？

问： 因为大家包括你然后包括 Jason 他出来经常会说 take care of others，就不管是员工还是外部的合作伙伴，这种 take care 是一种真实的吗？就是他真是这么想的吗？

答： 因为一开始的时候我们就是 We are producing design houses. We don't have any consumer products. We are using other companies to make GPU cards.

We have always had this habit of growing with the entire ecosystem. We make money together. We can't say that we are the only ones making money. We help make graphics cards, and other things都要一起往下走。

因为早期的显卡都是来做游戏，我们也不做个游戏。我们就是一直开发这些好的 library，帮助着游戏公司做游戏。我们刚开始走向 deep learning 的时候，那时候好几个框架，比如说 PyTorch, TensorFlow, 还有一些 MSNAMP 的一些东西，我们全部都支持。

那我觉得这也是他经营了这么多年，才把这个公司放在这么一个好的位置，让帮助别人也可以获得获利。这我觉得就是不容易。

六边形战士：Jensen 的多面性

问： 你近距离观察过老黄很多年，如果只用几个词来形容他，你会怎么形容啊？

答： 我们叫他六边形战士。就是不管是，我们有时候开会他可以走到很深去研究这个 register 这个 computer architecture register 这个非常细的细节，同时间又可以讲到讲到可以教大家怎么做 marketing 怎么做这些非常 high level 的东西。然后再处理这个不管是产品定价、然后跟客户的关系，面面俱到。

He is very enthusiastic. He gives everything he has to help the company be successful. This is a very admirable operation. He can make contributions in all aspects, and he does his best in all aspects. He is a very powerful person.

问： Does he encourage you more?

答： 批评比较多，一般来说。鼓励批评都有，当我还没有完全理解他要怎么去跑这个公司的时候，批评是比较多的。但批评总是带着鼓励。希望你可以变好。

他的目标就是 to torture everybody to greatness——经由这些磨练让你更加理解怎么样做才能做出不平凡的事情。这很好经历的。你愿意花时间去 torture 别人，这是件不容易的事情。所以 torture 别人，你自己心里要产生很大的负担，对吧？

Jensen 影响最深的一句话："Are you a quiet baby?"

问： 什么是让你印象最深刻的话？

答： 我记得有一次开会，We compared two solutions. I was doing one thing, and the other was doing something else. I remember I said that the setting they used was an unfair setting. So we didn't achieve our expectations in this aspect.

He said to me: "Are you a quiet baby? Nothing is fair in this world."

When you write a paper, you often say that your setting is different from yours, so you can't compare them at the same time. But if your goal is to solve a problem, then of course you have to do it according to the requirements of the problem solving. Without these requirements, you can't get it.

That sentence impressed me deeply. I am more strict in asking myself. 找理由是没有用的。give everything you have.

我以前也听过这句话，西点军校有一些著名的书也是讲的，就是没有理由 no excuse。但他跟我讲让我的印象就更加深刻，因为毕竟他是一个著名的人物。那我觉得这句话对我的印象也蛮大。我后来就不再找理由了。

生涯遗憾与"Number One"的定义

答： I can't define what number one is. I prefer to look at... Frontier model. Yes, but the Frontier model is the number one at that time. It's very successful, but there will be other models that can be made later.

I hope you have the ability to make the number one model. But [I didn't do it for nothing.]

问： Do you have any regrets in your research career? What else do you want to get?

答： I think I haven't succeeded physically. I haven't reached the point where I can talk about these things. I was very happy when I was in China 10 years ago. I was talking about how deep learning will replace computer graphics and become the most important image-oriented model. I was quite happy that this really happened.

I think this world model will be a major push to promote physical AI success. This is my next major goal. I hope this thing will also succeed.

你要比就是你有一个 Best Paper Award 你就会想说我要拿两个。然后我就照理说拿了十几个，总是拿不完嘛，对不对？比论文数总是有更多的论文。那你比 Citation 书总是有更多的 Citation。你比钱总是有人更多有钱，对不对？那重点是我觉得你对自己的东西是不是 proud of.

I think I didn't do well in the past, but I think I did well in the present. I accept it. I think I did what I was satisfied with within my capabilities. So many external criteria are not so important anymore, right？

对中国 AI 公司的观察

非常的 impressive, very impressive. 这些从 DeepSeek 开始啊，千问啊，豆包啊，我就把它全部夹进去吧。MiniMax，Jill，然后 Kimi 啊，然后这些 Nemo，委员，智谱，对，都做得很好。

那还有一件事情就是，在美国啊，尤其是 Frontier Lab, [很少 open source] to help to pass on these know-how. I think that the entire knowledge expansion, diffusion, is a good thing. Seeing these quickly develop, I think it's impressive.

答： I don't think it's purely hypnotized by LLM. It can't be denied that the most leading companies in AI right now, the most leading companies in the model, whether it's OpenAI or Swarovski, are all from large-language models.

This model is also clear. I don't know how to live without a coding agent now. I don't know if this is too convenient. I think it's a huge change. It's not a bad thing. LLM really has a great use. And it helps to improve our lives.

I think it's natural that people will think that this thing is already here. And what's the next step? I think people naturally think about what to do. I don't think there is such a thing as hypnosis. For those people, for the present time, it may be a very correct thing to do LLM.

Then new things will happen one after another. The company that was strong 100 years ago is completely different from the current one. 50 years ago is different, 20 years ago is different. I think as long as the organizational structure of this society is still in a good state of mind, there will be constant innovation.

The leading model has more time to find the way to distinguish. And then the powerful company can also add their own powerful ecosystem to make some changes.

I don't think that when software first came out, there were very few software companies. Now everyone writes software. Each software has its own way of distinguishing. I don't think there is a reason why the model is different. I think it will be the same.

So there is no need to mythologize model or model company?

I see it as a variety show. It's a black box. After so many different attempts, it's a set of questions. Many people will be in the variety show. The key is what you want to do with it. Yes, what do you want to do with it? Some people have deeper interpretation. Some people need more time.

每家公司都需要训练自己的大模型吗？

答： 你不觉得有必要？If it's commanding, do you need to build your own factory？

但是现在这个时代你可能不需要了，对吧？

答： 我觉得这东西在地质上从来没发生过，然后我不觉得对。因为人跟人相处没那么容易的。你看当初 Dario Amodei 跟 Sam Altman 就是合不来，对吧？他就走了。然后你最近在 Nemotron 里面每个人都是一模一样 [这不太可能]。

So everyone can do it. You have determination and you have resources. You can do it. So there is no need for that.

Cosmos 是"不能输的战争"吗？

问： Is Cosmos for you a war that you can't lose?

答： If there are other companies that also do open source models, then it's not. What is war? I didn't plan to kill anyone. I have to turn on this track. You all have to grow up in my body. NVIDIA continues to grow.

Physical AI is a major market. Now, there are no robots in every household. But if there are robots, my family may buy two or three. Every robot needs to be smart. That means the demand for smartness in the whole world will grow significantly. If this happens, it will be a huge benefit to the media.

Our mentality is not to kill people. Our mentality is how to build a market. CUDA is to build a market, to build the AI market today. We want to build the next big market. Then you say, can't we lose the battlefield? I think it's not because it's a brand new thing. We don't compete with anyone, right? Yeah, it's the power to build that market with everyone.

然后你卖这个机器人赚钱，你做这个 customer 赚钱，那这个东西会需要一些算力，赚钱，那当然会有公司研发自己的晶片，它也会赚钱，那整个市场就起来，原本是 nothing。
